title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第三十四 良政
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第三十四 良政 Volume 53 Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五十三‧列傳第三十四 良政

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53, Biographies 34: Good Governance
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53, Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 傅琰 虞愿 劉懷慰 裴昭明 沈憲 李珪之 孔琇之

translations.literal: Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Liu Huaiwei, Pei Zhaoming, Shen Xian, Li Guizhi, Kong Xiuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Liu Huaiwei, Pei Zhaoming, Shen Xian, Li Guizhi, and Kong Xiuzhi

sentences.zh: 太祖承宋氏奢縱，風移百城，輔立幼主，思振民瘼。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor inherited the Song dynasty's extravagance and excess; customs had shifted across a hundred cities; he aided in enthroning a young sovereign and sought to revive the people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor took over after the Song court's extravagance had spread its influence through countless cities. He helped place a young ruler on the throne and set out to relieve the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 爲政未朞，擢山陰令傅琰爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long in office, he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely begun to govern when he promoted Fu Yan, the magistrate of Shanyin, to Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 乃捐華反樸，恭己南面，導民以躬，意存勿擾。

translations.literal: He then abandoned splendor and returned to simplicity, holding himself with restraint as he faced south, leading the people by personal example, with intent not to disturb them.
translations.idiomatic: He cast off display for simplicity, held himself with restraint on the throne, led the people by his own example, and kept his mind set on leaving them undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 以山陰大邑，獄訟繁滋，建元三年，別置獄丞，與建康爲比。

translations.literal: Because Shanyin was a great prefecture with proliferating litigation, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison clerk was appointed, on par with Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shanyin was a major prefecture where lawsuits multiplied, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison clerk was installed there, on the same footing as Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 永明繼運，垂心治術。

translations.literal: During the Yongming reign he succeeded to the mandate and devoted attention to the art of governance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongming era began, he devoted himself to the craft of governing well.

sentences.zh: 杖威善斷，猶多漏網，長吏犯法，封刃行誅。

translations.literal: Relying on stern authority and sound judgments, yet many still slipped through the net; when senior officials violated the law, the blade was sealed and punishment carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with stern authority and sharp judgment, yet many offenders still escaped; when senior officials broke the law, the executioner's blade was drawn and sentence was carried out.

sentences.zh: 郡縣居職，以三周爲小滿。

translations.literal: For service in prefectural and county posts, three years constituted a minor term of completion.
translations.idiomatic: For service in prefectural and county office, three years counted as a completed term.

sentences.zh: 水旱之災，輙加賑卹。

translations.literal: In disasters of flood or drought, relief and succor were promptly added.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever flood or drought struck, relief and aid were promptly provided.

sentences.zh: 明帝自在布衣，曉達吏事，君臨億兆，專務刀筆，未嘗枉法申恩，守宰以之肅震。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, from his days in common dress, understood administrative affairs; when he ruled the myriad people he devoted himself to legal documents, never bending the law to grant favor, and prefects and magistrates were awed into reverence thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Even before he took the throne, Emperor Ming understood how government worked. Once he ruled the realm he lived by the written law, never twisting it to show favor, and officials throughout the land were awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 永明之世，十許年中，百姓無雞鳴犬吠之警，都邑之盛，士女富逸，歌聲舞節，袨服華粧，桃花綠水之間，秋月春風之下，蓋以百數。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, for some ten years the common people had no alarm even of crowing cocks or barking dogs; the capital's prosperity—ladies and gentlemen at ease in wealth, songs and dance, splendid dress and ornament, amid peach blossoms and green waters, under autumn moons and spring breezes—numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: For some ten years under Yongming the people knew no disturbance even of crowing cocks or barking dogs. The capital flourished: men and women lived in comfort and plenty, with song and dance, fine dress and ornament, amid peach blossoms and green waters, under autumn moons and spring breezes—such scenes numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 及建武之興，虜難猋急，征役連歲，不遑啓居，軍國糜耗，從此衰矣。

translations.literal: When the Jianwu era arose, barbarian troubles blew fierce; levies and corvée continued year on year; there was no leisure to open the door and dwell in peace; state and army were drained—and from this came decline.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwu era began, northern raids grew fierce. Levies and corvée dragged on year after year; people had no peace even at home. State and army were drained, and from that point the dynasty declined.

sentences.zh: 齊世善政著名表績無幾焉，位次遷升，非直止乎城邑。

translations.literal: Under the Qi, renowned good governance with manifest achievement was few; promotions in rank did not stop merely at city and town.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi there were few officials whose good governance won lasting fame. Many rose in rank beyond the level of city and county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 今取其清察有迹者，餘則隨以附焉。

translations.literal: Now we take those whose clarity and scrutiny left traces; the rest we append accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Here we record those whose integrity and sharp judgment left a clear record; the others are included as they follow.

sentences.zh: 傅琰字季珪，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Yan, courtesy name Jigui, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yan, courtesy name Jigui, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邵，員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was a Director of Administration.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao served as a Director of Administration.

sentences.zh: 父僧祐，安東錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Sengyou was Recorder of the Eastern Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengyou was Recorder under the Eastern Pacification command.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，遷山陰令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi he was transferred to be magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi he was appointed magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 山陰，東土大縣，難爲長官，僧祐在縣有稱，琰尤明察，又著能名。

translations.literal: Shanyin was a great county of the eastern lands, difficult to govern as chief; Sengyou had a reputation in the county, and Yan was especially keen in judgment, also winning a name for capability.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin was a major county in the east and a hard post for any magistrate. Sengyou had already won praise there, and Yan was especially sharp in judgment and soon gained a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 其年爵新亭侯。

translations.literal: That year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhui era he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，居南岸，隣家失火，延燒琰屋，琰抱柩不動，隣人競來赴救，乃得俱全。

translations.literal: When his mother died he dwelt on the south bank; a neighbor's fire spread and burned Yan's house; Yan embraced the coffin without moving; neighbors rushed to rescue and all was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he lived on the south bank. A neighbor's fire spread to his house, but Yan held the coffin and would not move. Neighbors rushed to help, and both he and the coffin were saved unharmed.

sentences.zh: 琰股髀之閒，已被煙焰。

translations.literal: Between Yan's thigh and buttock he had already been touched by smoke and flame.
translations.idiomatic: The flesh between his thigh and hip had already been scorched by smoke and flame.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除邵陵王左軍諮議，江夏王錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Consultative Officer of the Left Army under the Prince of Shaoling and Recorder under the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed consultative officer of the Left Army under the Prince of Shaoling and recorder under the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，以山陰獄訟煩積，復以琰爲山陰令。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor aided the government, because litigation in Shanyin had piled up, Yan was again made magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founding Emperor held power as regent, lawsuits in Shanyin had piled up, so Yan was again appointed magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 賣針賣糖老姥爭團絲，來詣琰，琰不辨覈，縳團絲於柱鞭之，密視有鐵屑，乃罰賣糖者。

translations.literal: Two old women, one selling needles and one selling sugar, disputed a ball of silk thread; they came to Yan; Yan did not investigate on the spot but tied the silk to a post and flogged it, secretly watching for iron filings, then punished the sugar-seller.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman who sold needles and one who sold sugar quarreled over a ball of silk and brought the case to Yan. Without questioning them at once, he tied the silk to a post and had it beaten, watching secretly for iron filings. When he found them, he punished the sugar-seller.

sentences.zh: 二野父爭雞，琰各問「何以食雞」，一人云「粟」，一人云「豆」，乃破雞得粟，罪言豆者。

translations.literal: Two peasants disputed a chicken; Yan asked each "what do you feed the chicken"; one said "millet," one said "beans"; he broke open the chicken and found millet, and convicted the one who said beans.
translations.idiomatic: Two peasants disputed ownership of a chicken. Yan asked each what he fed it; one said millet, the other beans. He slaughtered the bird and found millet in its crop, then convicted the man who had said beans.

sentences.zh: 縣內稱神明，無敢復爲偷盜。

translations.literal: Within the county he was called divine in judgment; none dared steal again.
translations.idiomatic: The county hailed him as uncannily perceptive in judgment, and no one dared steal again.

sentences.zh: 琰父子竝著奇績，江左鮮有。

translations.literal: Father and son Yan both achieved extraordinary records, rarely seen in the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son alike won extraordinary reputations as magistrates—rare in the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 世云「諸傅有《治縣譜》，子孫相傳，不以示人」。

translations.literal: It was said among the world that "the Fu clan has a Manual for Governing Counties, handed down among descendants and not shown to outsiders."
translations.idiomatic: People said that the Fu family kept a Manual for Governing Counties, passed down from generation to generation and never shown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 臨淮劉玄明亦有吏能，爲山陰令，大著名績。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanming of Linhuai also had administrative talent and served as Shanyin magistrate with great famous achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanming of Linhuai also had real talent for administration; as magistrate of Shanyin he won great fame for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 琰子翽問之，玄明曰：「我臨去當告卿。

translations.literal: Yan's son Lou asked him; Xuanming said: "When I am about to leave I shall tell you."
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Lou asked him for advice. Xuanming said, "When I am about to leave office I will tell you."

sentences.zh: 」將別，謂之曰：「作縣唯日食一升飰，而莫飲酒。」

translations.literal: " As they were parting he told him: "As magistrate eat only one sheng of rice per day, and do not drink wine."
translations.idiomatic: " At parting he said to him, "As magistrate, eat only one sheng of rice a day—and do not drink wine."

sentences.zh: 虞愿字士恭，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yuan, courtesy name Shigong, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan, courtesy name Shigong, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖賚，給事中，監利侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fen was a Palace Attendant and Marquis of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fen served as a Palace Attendant and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianli.

sentences.zh: 父望之，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Wangzhi died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wangzhi died while still young.

sentences.zh: 賚中庭橘樹冬熟，子孫競來取之，愿年數歲，獨不取，賚及家人皆異之。

translations.literal: An orange tree in the courtyard of Fen ripened in winter; descendants competed to pick the fruit; Yuan was only a few years old and alone did not take any; Fen and the whole family marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: An orange tree in Fen's courtyard ripened in winter, and the grandchildren rushed to pick the fruit. Yuan was only a few years old and alone refused to take any. Fen and the whole family were struck by this.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，爲國子生，再遷湘東王國常侍，轉潯陽王府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia he became a student of the Imperial University, was twice promoted to Regular Attendant of the Principality of Xiangdong, and transferred to Ink-Bureau Adjutant of the Principality of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanjia era he entered the Imperial University, was twice promoted to regular attendant in the Principality of Xiangdong, and then became ink-bureau adjutant in the Principality of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，以愿儒吏學涉，兼蕃國舊恩，意遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, because Yuan was a Confucian official of broad learning and also owed old favor from the princely house, he was treated with exceptional regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, he favored Yuan greatly—for his learning and skill as a scholar-official, and for old ties to the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 除太常丞，尚書祠部郎，通直散騎侍郎，領五郡中正，祠部郎如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, Director of the Sacrificial Affairs Section of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and concurrently Director of the Five-Commandery Rectification Bureau, retaining his post as Director of Sacrificial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, Director of the Sacrificial Affairs Section, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and concurrently head of the Five-Commandery Rectification Bureau, while keeping his post in the Sacrificial Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 帝性猜忌，體肥憎風，夏月常著皮小衣，拜左右二人爲司風令史，風起方面，輙先啓聞。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious by nature, corpulent and averse to wind; in summer he often wore a small leather garment; he appointed two attendants as Wind-Control Clerks, and whenever wind rose from any quarter they were to report it at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was suspicious by nature, heavy in build, and hated drafts. In summer he often wore a small leather vest. He appointed two attendants as Wind-Control Clerks who had to report at once whenever wind rose from any direction.

sentences.zh: 星文災變，不信太史，不聽外奏，勑靈臺知星二人給愿，常直內省，有異先啓，以相檢察。

translations.literal: For astral omens and calamities he did not trust the Grand Astrologer or heed outside reports; he ordered two star-knowers of the Observatory assigned to Yuan, who were to remain on duty within the inner palace, report any anomaly first, and keep each other in check.
translations.idiomatic: For celestial signs and disasters he distrusted the Grand Astrologer and would not hear outside reports. He assigned Yuan two Observatory astronomers who stayed on duty in the inner palace, reported any anomaly at once, and kept watch on each other.

sentences.zh: 帝以故宅起湘宮寺，費極奢侈。

translations.literal: The emperor built the Xiang Palace Temple on his former residence, at expense of extreme luxury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built the Xiang Palace Temple on the site of his former home, at ruinous expense.

sentences.zh: 以孝武莊嚴剎七層，帝欲起十層，不可立，分爲兩剎，各五層。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had seven stories, the emperor wished to build ten; this could not stand, so it was divided into two monasteries of five stories each.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had seven stories; the emperor wanted ten, but the structure would not bear it, so he built two monasteries of five stories each.

sentences.zh: 新安太守巢尚之罷郡還，見帝，曰：「卿至湘宮寺未？

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi, Grand Administrator of Xin'an, having left his post and returned, saw the emperor and said: "Have you been to the Xiang Palace Temple?"
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shangzhi of Xin'an, having left office and returned to court, asked the emperor, "Have you been to the Xiang Palace Temple yet?"

sentences.zh: 我起此寺，是大功德。

translations.literal: I built this temple—it is a great meritorious deed.
translations.idiomatic: "I built this temple. It is a great act of merit."

sentences.zh: 」愿在側曰：「陛下起此寺，皆是百姓賣兒貼婦錢，佛若有知，當悲哭哀愍，罪高佛圖，有何功德？

translations.literal: " Yuan, standing beside him, said: "Your Majesty, this temple was built entirely with money from common people selling their sons and pawning their wives. If the Buddha had knowledge, he would weep in grief and pity; the sin towers higher than the Buddhist pagoda—what merit is there?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan, standing at his side, said, "Your Majesty, this temple was paid for with money wrung from people who sold their children and pawned their wives. If the Buddha could see it, he would weep in pity. The sin rises higher than the pagoda—where is the merit in that?"

sentences.zh: 」尚書令袁粲在坐，爲之失色。

translations.literal: " Yuan Can, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was present and turned pale at this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Can, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, who was present, turned pale.

sentences.zh: 帝乃怒，使人驅下殿，愿徐去無異容。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and had men drive him from the hall; Yuan withdrew slowly without change of expression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had him driven from the hall. Yuan withdrew slowly, his face unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以舊恩，少日中，已復召入。

translations.literal: Because of old favor, before midday he was summoned in again.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to their old bond, before noon he had been summoned back.

sentences.zh: 帝好圍碁，甚拙，去格七八道，物議共欺爲第三品。

translations.literal: The emperor loved weiqi but played very poorly, leaving seven or eight lines from the grid; public opinion together deceived him into thinking he was third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved weiqi but played very badly, often leaving seven or eight lines of the board empty. Court opinion humored him into believing he ranked third class.

sentences.zh: 與第一品王抗圍碁，依品賭戲，抗每饒借之，曰：「皇帝飛碁，臣抗不能斷。

translations.literal: He played weiqi with Wang Kang of first rank, wagering by rank; Kang always let him win and said: "The emperor's stones fly; your servant Kang cannot cut them off."
translations.idiomatic: He played weiqi with Wang Kang, ranked first class, wagering by rank. Kang always let him win, saying, "The emperor's stones fly like lightning; this servant cannot cut them off."

sentences.zh: 」帝終不覺，以爲信然，好之愈篤。

translations.literal: " The emperor never perceived the truth, believed it sincerely, and loved the game all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor never caught on, took it all as truth, and grew even fonder of the game.

sentences.zh: 愿又曰：「堯以此教丹朱，非人主所宜好也。

translations.literal: Yuan also said: "Yao used this to teach Danzhu—it is not what a ruler ought to love."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan also said, "Yao used this game to teach his son Danzhu. It is not a pastime a ruler should indulge in."

sentences.zh: 」雖數忤旨，而蒙賞賜，猶異餘人。

translations.literal: " Though he often offended the imperial will, he still received rewards unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: " Though he often spoke against the emperor's wishes, he was still rewarded more generously than others.

sentences.zh: 遷兼中書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to concurrent Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent Attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，愿常侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the emperor took to his bed with illness, Yuan constantly attended him with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill, Yuan stayed at his side to tend his medical care.

sentences.zh: 帝素能食，尤好逐夷，以銀缽盛蜜漬之，一食數缽。

translations.literal: The emperor had always been able to eat heartily and especially loved zhuyi preserved fish; he kept it in a silver bowl steeped in honey and ate several bowls at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always been a hearty eater and was especially fond of zhuyi, a preserved fish delicacy kept in silver bowls steeped in honey; he could eat several bowls in one sitting.

sentences.zh: 謂揚州刺史王景文曰：「此是奇味，卿頗足不？

translations.literal: He said to Wang Jingwen, Inspector of Yangzhou: "This is a rare delicacy—do you have enough of it?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Wang Jingwen, Inspector of Yangzhou, "This is a rare delicacy. Do you ever get enough of it?"

sentences.zh: 」景文曰：「臣夙好此物，貧素致之甚難。

translations.literal: " Jingwen said: "Your servant has long loved this food, but in poverty and plain living it is very hard to obtain."
translations.idiomatic: " Jingwen replied, "I have always loved it, but in my humble circumstances it is very hard to come by."

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 食逐夷積多，胷腹痞脹，氣將絕。

translations.literal: From eating too much zhuyi his chest and belly became congested and swollen, and his breath was nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: He ate so much zhuyi that his chest and belly swelled with blockage, and he was near death.

sentences.zh: 左右啓飲數升酢酒，乃消。

translations.literal: Those beside him advised drinking several sheng of vinegar wine, and the swelling subsided.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants had him drink several sheng of vinegar wine, and the swelling eased.

sentences.zh: 疾大困，一食汁滓猶至三升，水患積久，藥不復效。

translations.literal: When the illness grew severe, a single meal of broth and dregs still reached three sheng; water retention had accumulated long, and medicine no longer worked.
translations.idiomatic: As the illness worsened, he still took as much as three sheng of broth and sediment at a meal. Edema had built up over time, and medicine no longer helped.

sentences.zh: 大漸日，正坐，呼道人，合掌便絕。

translations.literal: On the day of his final decline he sat upright, called for a Daoist priest, joined his palms, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he was failing fast he sat upright, summoned a Daoist priest, joined his palms, and died.

sentences.zh: 愿以侍疾久，轉正員郎。

translations.literal: Because Yuan had long attended the sick emperor, he was transferred to regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuan had long attended him in illness, he was promoted to regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉平太守，在郡不治生產。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Jinping and in the commandery did not pursue personal profit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Jinping and made no effort to enrich himself in office.

sentences.zh: 前政與民交關，質錄其兒婦，愿遣人於道奪取將還。

translations.literal: The previous administrator had dealings with the people and held a man's daughter-in-law as pledge; Yuan sent men on the road to seize her back and return her.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had taken a commoner's daughter-in-law as security for a debt. Yuan sent men to intercept her on the road and bring her back.

sentences.zh: 在郡立學堂教授。

translations.literal: In the commandery he established a school and taught.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he founded a school and taught there.

sentences.zh: 郡舊出髯蛇膽，可爲藥，有餉愿蛇者，愿不忍殺，放二十里外山中，一夜蛇還牀下。

translations.literal: The commandery traditionally produced bearded-snake gall usable as medicine; when someone presented Yuan with a snake, he could not bear to kill it and released it twenty li into the mountains; in one night the snake returned beneath his bed.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was known for bearded-snake gall used in medicine. When someone brought Yuan a live snake, he could not bear to kill it and released it twenty li into the hills—but overnight the snake was back under his bed.

sentences.zh: 復送四十里外山，經宿，復還故處。

translations.literal: He sent it again forty li into the mountains; after a night it returned to the same place.
translations.idiomatic: He released it again forty li away, but after another night it returned to the same spot.

sentences.zh: 愿更令遠，乃不復歸，論者以爲仁心所致也。

translations.literal: Yuan had it taken still farther, and then it did not return; commentators held that this came from his humane heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had it taken even farther off, and then it did not return. Commentators said this showed the power of his compassionate nature.

sentences.zh: 海邊有越王石，常隱雲霧。

translations.literal: By the seashore there was a Yue King's Stone, usually hidden in cloud and mist.
translations.idiomatic: On the coast stood a stone called the Yue King's Stone, usually shrouded in mist.

sentences.zh: 相傳云：「清廉太守乃得見。

translations.literal: Tradition said: "Only an incorrupt Grand Administrator can see it."
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that only an incorrupt magistrate could see it clearly.

sentences.zh: 」愿往觀視，清徹無隱蔽。

translations.literal: " Yuan went to look, and it was clear and without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yuan went to look, the stone stood clear, with nothing hidden.

sentences.zh: 後琅邪王秀之爲郡，與朝士書曰：「此郡承虞公之後，善政猶存，遺風易遵，差得無事。

translations.literal: Later when Wang Xiuzhi of Langye governed the commandery, he wrote to court gentlemen: "This commandery, following upon Lord Yu, still has good governance; the legacy is easy to follow, and affairs are more or less untroubled."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Xiuzhi of Langye took the post, he wrote to colleagues at court, "This commandery still bears the mark of Lord Yu's good rule. His legacy is easy to follow, and affairs are largely untroubled."

sentences.zh: 」以母老解職，除後軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Because his mother was old he resigned his post and was appointed General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: " When his mother grew old he resigned and was appointed General of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 褚淵常詣愿，不在，見其眠牀上積塵埃，有書數袠。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan often called on Yuan; when Yuan was not in, he saw dust piled on the sleeping couch and several bundles of books.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan often visited Yuan. Once when Yuan was out, he saw dust thick on the bed and several bundles of books lying there.

sentences.zh: 淵歎曰：「虞君之清，一至於此。

translations.literal: Chu sighed and said: "Lord Yu's purity reaches even to this."
translations.idiomatic: Chu sighed and said, "Lord Yu's integrity goes even this far."

sentences.zh: 」令人掃地拂牀而去。

translations.literal: " He had someone sweep the floor and dust the couch, then left.
translations.idiomatic: " He had someone sweep the floor and dust the bed, then left.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，領東觀祭酒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Central Secretariat and concurrently Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant of the Central Secretariat and concurrently Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 兄季，爲上虞令，卒。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ji was magistrate of Shangyu and died.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ji, magistrate of Shangyu, died.

sentences.zh: 愿從省步還家，不待詔便歸東。

translations.literal: Yuan left the Secretariat on foot and returned home, not waiting for an edict but going east at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan left the Secretariat on foot for home, not waiting for imperial permission before returning east.

sentences.zh: 除驍騎將軍，遷廷尉，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, promoted to Minister of Justice, and retained his post as Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, then promoted to Minister of Justice, while keeping his post as Libationer.

sentences.zh: 愿嘗事宋明帝，齊初宋神主遷汝陰廟，愿拜辭流涕。

translations.literal: Yuan had once served Emperor Ming of Song; at the beginning of Qi, when the Song imperial tablets were moved to the Ruyin temple, Yuan bowed in farewell with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had long served Emperor Ming of Song. When the Qi dynasty began and the Song imperial spirit tablets were moved to the temple at Ruyin, he bowed in farewell with tears streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 年五十四。

translations.literal: He was fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 愿著《五經論問》，撰《會稽記》，文翰數十篇。

translations.literal: Yuan authored Discussions and Questions on the Five Classics, compiled Records of Kuaiji, and several dozen pieces of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wrote Discussions and Questions on the Five Classics, compiled Records of Kuaiji, and left several dozen other literary works.

sentences.zh: 劉懷慰字彥泰，平原平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Huaiwei, courtesy name Yantai, was a native of Pingyuan in Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaiwei, courtesy name Yantai, was a native of Pingyuan in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖奉伯，元嘉中，爲冠軍長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fengbo, during Yuanjia, was Chief Clerk of the Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fengbo served during the Yuanjia era as chief clerk to the Champion General.

sentences.zh: 父乘民，冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chengmin was Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengmin was Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 懷慰初爲桂陽王征北板行參軍。

translations.literal: Huaiwei first served as Acting Adjutant on the Northern Campaign staff board of the Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwei began as acting adjutant on the northern campaign staff of the Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 乘民死於義嘉事難，懷慰持喪，不食醯醬，冬月不絮衣。

translations.literal: Chengmin died in the Yijia troubles; Huaiwei observed mourning, ate no pickled sauces, and in winter wore no padded garments.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmin died in the troubles of the Yijia era. Huaiwei mourned him without eating pickled foods and, even in winter, wore no padded clothes.

sentences.zh: 養孤弟妹，事寡叔母，皆有恩義。

translations.literal: He raised orphaned younger siblings, served his widowed aunt by marriage—all with kindness and duty.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his orphaned younger siblings and cared for his widowed aunt by marriage, showing kindness and duty in both.

sentences.zh: 復除邵陵王南中郎參軍，廣德令，尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Adjutant of the Southern Central Army under the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and Director of the Chariot Section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed adjutant of the Southern Central Army under the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and Director of the Chariot Section.

sentences.zh: 懷慰宗從善明等，太祖心腹，懷慰亦豫焉。

translations.literal: Huaiwei's clansmen Shanming and others were trusted intimates of the Founding Emperor, and Huaiwei was also among them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwei's kinsmen Shanming and others were trusted intimates of the Founding Emperor, and Huaiwei was counted among them as well.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之有舊，令爲書戒喻攸之，太祖省之稱善。

translations.literal: He had old ties with Shen Youzhi and was ordered to write a letter admonishing Youzhi; the Founding Emperor read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He had old ties with Shen Youzhi and was told to write a letter warning him. The Founding Emperor read it and praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，上欲置齊郡於京邑，議者以江右土沃，流民所歸，乃治瓜步，以懷慰爲輔國將軍、齊郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, the sovereign wished to place Qi commandery in the capital region; debaters held that the lands south of the Yangzi were fertile and where displaced people gathered, so administration was set at Guabu, and Huaiwei was made General Who Supports the State and Grand Administrator of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi state was founded, the ruler wanted to place Qi commandery in the capital region. Advisers argued that the lands south of the Yangzi were fertile and drew displaced people, so the seat was established at Guabu, and Huaiwei was made General Who Supports the State and Grand Administrator of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 上謂懷慰曰：「齊邦是王業所基，吾方以爲顯任。

translations.literal: The sovereign said to Huaiwei: "The Qi domain is the foundation of our royal enterprise; I regard this as a conspicuous appointment."
translations.idiomatic: The ruler said to Huaiwei, "The Qi domain is the foundation of our royal enterprise. I mean this as a post of real consequence."

sentences.zh: 經理之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: All matters of administration I entrust entirely to you.
translations.idiomatic: I entrust all matters of governance entirely to you.

sentences.zh: 」又手勑曰：「有文事者，必有武備。

translations.literal: " He also wrote in his own hand: "Where there are civil affairs, there must also be military preparedness."
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote in his own hand, "Where there are civil affairs, there must be military preparedness as well."

sentences.zh: 今賜卿玉環刀一口。

translations.literal: Now I bestow on you one jade-ringed blade."
translations.idiomatic: I now bestow on you a jade-ringed saber."

sentences.zh: 」懷慰至郡，修治城郭，安集居民，墾廢田二百頃，決沈湖灌溉。

translations.literal: " When Huaiwei reached the commandery he repaired walls and moats, settled the people, reclaimed two hundred qing of abandoned fields, and opened the Shen Lake for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: " When Huaiwei took office he repaired the walls, settled the people, reclaimed two hundred qing of abandoned farmland, and opened the Shen Lake for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 不受禮謁，民有餉其新米一斛者，懷慰出所食麥飯示之，曰：「旦食有餘，幸不煩此。

translations.literal: He accepted no gifts or calls of courtesy; when a commoner presented him with one hu of new rice, Huaiwei brought out the barley meal he was eating and showed it, saying: "My morning meal already leaves a surplus—please do not trouble yourself with this."
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no gifts. When a commoner brought him a hu of new rice, Huaiwei showed him the barley meal he was eating and said, "I already have enough for breakfast—please do not trouble yourself."

sentences.zh: 」因著《廉吏論》以達其意。

translations.literal: " He then wrote On Incorrupt Officials to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote On Incorrupt Officials to make his views known.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，手勑褒賞。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor heard of this, he wrote in his own hand to praise and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor heard of it, he wrote in his own hand to praise and reward him.

sentences.zh: 進督秦、沛二郡。

translations.literal: He was advanced to oversee Qin and Pei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to oversee Qin and Pei commanderies as well.

sentences.zh: 妻子在都，賜米三百斛。

translations.literal: His wife and children were in the capital; he was granted three hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Because his wife and children remained in the capital, he was granted three hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 兖州刺史柳世隆與懷慰書曰：「膠東淵化，潁川致美，以今方古，曾何足云。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong, Inspector of Yanzhou, wrote to Huaiwei: "Jiaodong's deep transformation and Yingchuan's attainment of beauty—compared with the present, what of the past is worth mentioning?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong, Inspector of Yanzhou, wrote to Huaiwei, "Jiaodong's deep civilizing influence and Yingchuan's celebrated excellence—set against your work today, what can the ancients even claim?"

sentences.zh: 」在郡二年，遷正員郎，領青冀二州中正。

translations.literal: " After two years in the commandery he was transferred to regular Attendant and concurrently headed the Rectification Bureau for Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: " After two years in office he was promoted to regular Attendant and made head of the Rectification Bureau for Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 懷慰本名聞慰，世祖卽位，以與舅氏名同，勑改之。

translations.literal: Huaiwei's original name was Wenwei; when Emperor Wu took the throne, because it was the same as his maternal uncle's name, an edict changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwei had originally been named Wenwei. When Emperor Wu came to the throne, the name matched that of his maternal uncle, so an edict changed it.

sentences.zh: 出監東陽郡，爲吏民所安。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise Dongyang commandery and was a source of security for officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to supervise Dongyang commandery, where officials and commoners alike found security under his rule.

sentences.zh: 還兼安陸王北中郎司馬。

translations.literal: On returning he concurrently served as Marshal of the Northern Central Army under the Prince of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he concurrently served as marshal of the Northern Central Army under the Prince of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Yongming.

sentences.zh: 年四十五。

translations.literal: He was forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，謂僕射徐孝嗣曰：「劉懷慰若在，朝廷不憂無清吏也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he said to Director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi: "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would not worry about lacking incorrupt officials."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, he told Xu Xiaosi, Director of the Secretariat, "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would never lack incorrupt officials."

sentences.zh: 」懷慰與濟陽江淹、陳郡袁彖善，亦著文翰。

translations.literal: " Huaiwei was on good terms with Jiang Yan of Jiyang and Yuan Can of Chen commandery, and also produced literary writings.
translations.idiomatic: " Huaiwei was close to Jiang Yan of Jiyang and Yuan Can of Chen commandery, and also left literary works.

sentences.zh: 永明初，獻《皇德論》云。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he presented On Imperial Virtue, which read in part:
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongming he presented his treatise On Imperial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 裴昭明，河東聞喜人，宋太中大夫松之孫也。

translations.literal: Pei Zhaoming was a native of Wenxi in Hedong and grandson of Song's Grand Master of Palace Counsel Pei Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhaoming was a native of Wenxi in Hedong and grandson of Pei Songzhi, Grand Master of Palace Counsel under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父駰，南中郎參軍。

translations.literal: His father Yin was Adjutant of the Southern Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin served as adjutant of the Southern Central Army.

sentences.zh: 昭明少傳儒史之業。

translations.literal: Zhaoming from youth inherited the work of Confucian learning and historical studies.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhaoming inherited the family tradition of classical learning and historical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，爲太學博士。

translations.literal: During Taishi he was a Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era he served as an Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「太子婚，納徵用玉璧虎皮，未詳何所准據。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "For the crown prince's marriage, the presentation of betrothal gifts uses jade disks and tiger skins; it is unclear on what authority this rests."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported, "For the crown prince's wedding, betrothal gifts include jade disks and tiger skins, but the authority for this is unclear."

sentences.zh: 」昭明議：「禮納徵，儷皮爲庭實，鹿皮也。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming argued: "In ritual, betrothal gifts use paired skins as court offerings—deer skin."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming argued, "According to ritual, betrothal gifts use paired hides as court offerings—and those hides should be deerskin."

sentences.zh: 晉太子納妃注『以虎皮二』。

translations.literal: The Jin commentary on the crown prince taking a consort reads 'two tiger skins.'
translations.idiomatic: A Jin commentary on the crown prince taking a consort reads, "two tiger skins."

sentences.zh: 太元中，公主納徵，虎豹皮各一。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era, for a princess's betrothal gifts, one tiger skin and one leopard skin were each used.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan era, when a princess received betrothal gifts, one tiger skin and one leopard skin were used.

sentences.zh: 豈其謂婚禮不詳。

translations.literal: Can this mean that marriage rites are not fully specified?
translations.idiomatic: Surely this does not mean that marriage rites are left unspecified.

sentences.zh: 王公之差，故取虎豹文蔚以尊其事。

translations.literal: The difference for princes and dukes is why tiger and leopard, splendid in pattern, are taken to honor the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: For princes and dukes the distinction lies in using tiger and leopard skins, splendid in pattern, to honor the occasion.

sentences.zh: 虎豹雖文，而徵禮所不言，熊羆雖古，而婚禮所不及，珪璋雖美，或爲用各異。

translations.literal: Tiger and leopard, though patterned, are not mentioned in betrothal ritual; bear and brown bear, though ancient, are not covered in marriage rites; jade tablets, though beautiful, may serve differing uses.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger and leopard skins may be splendid, but betrothal ritual does not mention them; bear skins may be ancient precedents, but marriage rites do not include them; jade tablets may be beautiful, yet their uses differ.

sentences.zh: 今宜准的經誥，凡諸僻謬，一皆詳正。

translations.literal: Now we should take the classics and edicts as standard and examine and correct every irregularity in full.
translations.idiomatic: We should now take the classics and canonical edicts as our standard and examine and correct every irregular practice.

sentences.zh: 」於是有司參議，加珪璋，豹熊羆皮各二。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the relevant offices deliberated and added jade tablets and two each of leopard, bear, and brown-bear skins.
translations.idiomatic: " The relevant offices then deliberated and added jade tablets, plus two each of leopard, bear, and brown-bear skins.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，出爲長沙郡丞，罷任，刺史王蘊謂之曰：「卿清貧，必無還資。

translations.literal: During Yuanhui he went out as Assistant Administrator of Changsha commandery; when he left office, Inspector Wang Yun said to him: "You are poor and pure—you surely have no returning wealth."
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhui he served as assistant administrator of Changsha. When he left office, Inspector Wang Yun told him, "You are incorrupt and poor—you surely have no wealth to take home."

sentences.zh: 湘中人士有須一禮之命者，我不愛也。

translations.literal: If any gentleman of the Xiang region needs a single gift of office, I do not begrudge it."
translations.idiomatic: If any gentleman in the Xiang region needs a small gift from my office, I will not begrudge it."

sentences.zh: 」昭明曰：「下官忝爲邦佐，不能光益上府，豈以鴻都之事仰累清風。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming said: "Your humble servant is unworthily a commandery assistant and cannot brighten and benefit the superior prefecture—how could I burden your pure reputation with Hongdu-style affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming replied, "I am unworthy to serve as your assistant and cannot bring credit to your prefecture. How could I burden your integrity with such favors?"

sentences.zh: 」歷祠部通直郎。

translations.literal: " He served successively as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Sacrificial Affairs Section.
translations.idiomatic: " He later served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Sacrificial Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，使虜，世祖謂之曰：「以卿有將命之才，使還，當以一郡相賞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he was envoy to the barbarians; Emperor Wu said to him: "Because you have the talent to bear imperial commission, when you return I shall reward you with a commandery."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming he was sent as envoy to the northern court. Emperor Wu told him, "You have the talent to carry out a diplomatic mission. When you return, I shall reward you with a commandery."

sentences.zh: 」還爲始安內史。

translations.literal: " On his return he became Interior Secretary of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return he was appointed Interior Secretary of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 郡民龔玄宣，云神人與其玉印玉板書，不須筆，吹紙便成字。

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Gong Xuanyuan, claimed that a spirit gave him jade seals and jade boards for writing; without brush, by blowing on paper characters formed at once.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery resident named Gong Xuanyuan claimed that a spirit had given him jade seals and writing tablets; without a brush, he could blow on paper and characters would appear.

sentences.zh: 自稱「龔聖人」，以此惑衆。

translations.literal: He called himself "the Sage Gong" and by this deluded the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He called himself "the Sage Gong" and used this to mislead the people.

sentences.zh: 前後郡守敬事之，昭明付獄治罪。

translations.literal: Former and later commandery chiefs had honored him; Zhaoming handed him to prison for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Previous administrators had honored him, but Zhaoming had him imprisoned and punished.

sentences.zh: 及還，甚貧罄。

translations.literal: When he returned he was utterly destitute.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he was utterly destitute.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「裴昭明罷郡還，遂無宅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: "Pei Zhaoming left his commandery and returned without even a house."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu remarked, "Pei Zhaoming left office and came back without even owning a house."

sentences.zh: 我不諳書，不知古人中誰比？

translations.literal: I am not versed in books—among the ancients, to whom may he be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: I am no scholar—among the ancients, who does he resemble?"

sentences.zh: 」遷射聲校尉。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Commandant of the Archers.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Commandant of the Archers.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣北使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again sent as envoy to the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was again sent as envoy to the northern court.

sentences.zh: 建武初，爲王玄邈安北長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he served Wang Xuanmiao as Chief Clerk of the Northern Pacification and Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianwu he served as chief clerk of the Northern Pacification under Wang Xuanmiao and as Grand Administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 明帝以其在事無所啓奏，代還，責之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, because during his tenure he made no memorials, replaced and recalled him and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming recalled and replaced him because he had filed no memorials while in office, and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 昭明曰：「臣不欲競執關楗故耳。

translations.literal: Zhaoming said: "Your servant did not wish to compete over holding the gate-bars, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming replied, "I simply did not wish to wrangle over who held the keys to power."

sentences.zh: 」昭明歷郡皆有勤績，常謂人曰：「人生何事須聚蓄，一身之外，亦復何須？

translations.literal: " Zhaoming in every commandery had diligent achievement and often told people: "In life why must one amass stores? Beyond one's own person, what more is needed?"
translations.idiomatic: " In every post Zhaoming achieved solid results. He often said, "What need has life of hoarded wealth? Beyond one's own person, what more is required?"

sentences.zh: 子孫若不才，我聚彼散；

translations.literal: If descendants lack talent, what I gather they will scatter;
translations.idiomatic: If my descendants lack talent, what I gather they will squander;

sentences.zh: 若能自立，則不如一經。

translations.literal: if they can stand on their own, then one classic is better."
translations.idiomatic: if they can stand on their own, one classic text is worth more than any fortune."

sentences.zh: 」故終身不治產業。

translations.literal: " Therefore throughout his life he did not manage estates.
translations.idiomatic: " For that reason he never built up an estate in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟顗，字彥齊。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Yan, courtesy name Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Yan, courtesy name Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 少有異操。

translations.literal: From youth he had an unusual bearing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed an unusual character.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，於總明觀聽講，不讓劉秉席，秉用爲參軍。

translations.literal: During Taishi, at lectures in the Zongming Observatory, he would not yield his seat to Liu Bing; Bing employed him as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi, at lectures in the Zongming Observatory, he refused to yield his seat to Liu Bing, who then took him on as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 昇明末，爲奉朝請。

translations.literal: At the end of Shengming he was a Court Gentleman in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Shengming era he served as a Court Gentleman in Attendance.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，世子裴妃須外戚譜，顗不與，遂分籍。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, the heir apparent's Pei consort needed a maternal-kin genealogy; Yan would not provide it, and they therefore split registers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established, the crown prince's Pei consort needed a genealogy of maternal kin. Yan refused to supply it, and the families split their registers.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，上表誹謗，掛冠去，伏誅。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, Yan submitted a memorial of slander, hung up his cap and left, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication, Yan submitted a slanderous memorial, resigned his office, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 沈憲字彥璋，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Xian, courtesy name Yanzhang, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xian, courtesy name Yanzhang, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖說道，巴西梓潼二郡太守，父璞之，北中郎行參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuodao was Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong; his father Puzhi was Acting Adjutant of the Northern Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuodao served as Grand Administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies; his father Puzhi was acting adjutant of the Northern Central Army.

sentences.zh: 憲初應州辟，爲主簿。

translations.literal: Xian at first answered a provincial summons and became chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xian first answered a provincial summons and became chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 少有幹局，歷臨首、餘杭令，巴陵王府佐，帶襄令，除駕部郎。

translations.literal: From youth he had administrative capacity; he served as magistrate of Linshou and Yuhang, staff officer of the Principality of Baling, concurrently magistrate of Xiang, and was appointed Director of the Chariot Section.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed administrative talent. He served as magistrate of Linshou and Yuhang, as staff officer to the Prince of Baling while concurrently magistrate of Xiang, and was appointed Director of the Chariot Section.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝與憲棋，謂憲曰：「卿，廣州刺史才也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song played weiqi with Xian and said to him: "You have the talent of a Governor of Guangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song played weiqi with Xian and told him, "You have the makings of a Governor of Guangzhou."

sentences.zh: 」補烏程令，甚著政績。

translations.literal: " He was appointed magistrate of Wucheng and achieved very marked administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed magistrate of Wucheng and won a strong reputation for his achievements in office.

sentences.zh: 太守褚淵歎之曰：「此人方員可施。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Chu Yuan sighed and said: "This man is square and round as needed—he can be deployed anywhere."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Chu Yuan sighed and said, "This man adapts to any shape required—he can be put to use anywhere."

sentences.zh: 」除通直郎，都水使者。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commissioner of Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commissioner of Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 長於吏事，居官有績。

translations.literal: He excelled in administrative affairs and in office had achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in administrative work and achieved solid results in every post.

sentences.zh: 除正員郎，補吳令，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed regular Attendant, supplemented as magistrate of Wu, and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regular Attendant, then magistrate of Wu, and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，西中郎將晃爲豫州，太祖擢憲爲晃長史，南梁太守，行州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, when General of the Western Central Army Huang was in Yuzhou, the Founding Emperor promoted Xian to be Huang's Chief Clerk, Grand Administrator of Nanliang, and acting provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming, when General Huang of the Western Central Army held Yuzhou, the Founding Emperor made Xian his chief clerk, Grand Administrator of Nanliang, and acting head of provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷豫章王諮議，未拜，坐事免官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Consultative Officer under the Prince of Yuzhang; before taking office he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to consultative officer under the Prince of Yuzhang, but before taking office he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 復除安成王冠軍、武陵王征虜參軍，遷少府卿。

translations.literal: He was again appointed adjutant to the Champion General under the Prince of Ancheng and to the Barbarian-quelling General under the Prince of Wuling, then promoted to Minister of the Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed adjutant under the Prince of Ancheng and the Prince of Wuling, then promoted to Minister of the Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 少府管掌市易，與民交關，有吏能者，皆更此職。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Palace Supplies oversaw market exchange and dealings with the people; those with administrative talent were all rotated through this post.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Palace Supplies oversaw market trade and dealings with the people, and officials known for administrative talent were routinely assigned there.

sentences.zh: 遷王儉鎮軍長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army under Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as chief clerk of the Pacification Army under Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄爲會稽，以憲爲左軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Ye was in Kuaiji, Xian was made Marshal of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling Ye governed Kuaiji, Xian was appointed marshal of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 太祖以山陰戶衆難治，欲分爲兩縣。

translations.literal: Because Shanyin had a large population and was hard to govern, the Founding Emperor wished to divide it into two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shanyin's population was large and hard to govern, the Founding Emperor wanted to split it into two counties.

sentences.zh: 世祖啓曰：「縣豈不可治，但用不得其人耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu memorialized: "A county can surely be governed—the trouble is only that the right man is not used."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu replied, "A county can be governed—the problem is simply putting the wrong man in charge."

sentences.zh: 」乃以憲帶山陰令，政聲大著。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xian was made concurrent magistrate of Shanyin, and his governmental reputation became greatly noted.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian was then made concurrent magistrate of Shanyin, and his reputation for good governance spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 孔稚珪請假東歸，謂人曰：「沈令料事特有天才。

translations.literal: Kong Zhigui asked leave to return east and told people: "Magistrate Shen has a special genius for sizing up affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhigui took leave to return east and told people, "Magistrate Shen has a rare genius for judging affairs."

sentences.zh: 」加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: " He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 王敬則爲會稽，憲仍留爲鎮軍長史，令如故。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze was in Kuaiji, Xian remained as Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army, his magistracy unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze took over Kuaiji, Xian remained chief clerk of the Pacification Army while keeping his magistracy.

sentences.zh: 遷爲冠軍長史，行南豫州事，晉安王後軍長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Champion General, acting Southern Yuzhou affairs, Chief Clerk of the Rear Army under the Prince of Jin'an, and Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Champion General with acting authority over Southern Yuzhou, then served as chief clerk of the Rear Army under the Prince of Jin'an and as Grand Administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明代爲南兖州，憲仍留爲冠軍長史，太守如故，頻行州府事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xiyang Ziming replaced him in Southern Yanzhou, Xian remained Chief Clerk of the Champion General with his grand-administratorship unchanged, frequently conducting provincial and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xiyang Ziming took Southern Yanzhou, Xian remained chief clerk of the Champion General and kept his post as grand administrator, often handling provincial and prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，子明典籤劉道濟取府州五十人役自給，又役子明左右，及船仗贓私百萬，爲有司所奏，世祖怒，賜道濟死。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's registrar Liu Daoji took fifty men from the prefecture and commandery for his own service, also impressed Ziming's attendants, and in ships and arms had private graft of a million—reported by the relevant offices; Emperor Wu was angry and ordered Daoji to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's registrar Liu Daoji impressed fifty men from the prefecture and commandery for his own use, also conscripted the prince's attendants, and embezzled a million in ships and arms. When the relevant offices reported this, Emperor Wu was furious and had Daoji put to death.

sentences.zh: 憲坐不糾，免官。

translations.literal: Xian was punished for failing to investigate and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was dismissed for failing to investigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 尋復爲長史、輔國將軍，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Chief Clerk and General Who Supports the State, then left office because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed chief clerk and General Who Supports the State, but then resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 當世稱爲良吏。

translations.literal: His contemporaries called him a good official.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries hailed him as an excellent official.

sentences.zh: 憲同郡丘仲起，先是爲晉平郡，清廉自立。

translations.literal: Qiu Zhongqi of the same commandery as Xian had earlier governed Jinping commandery with purity and self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongqi, a fellow townsman of Xian, had earlier governed Jinping commandery with incorrupt integrity.

sentences.zh: 褚淵歎曰：「見可欲心能不亂，此楊公所以遺子孫也。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan sighed and said: "To see what one desires yet keep the heart unperturbed—this is why Lord Yang left his teaching to descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan sighed and said, "To see temptation yet keep one's heart steady—that is the lesson Lord Yang left his descendants."

sentences.zh: 」仲起字子震，少爲憲從伯領軍寅之所知。

translations.literal: " Zhongqi, courtesy name Zizhen, from youth was known to Xian's father's cousin, Commander-in-Chief Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongqi, courtesy name Zizhen, was known from youth to Xian's father's cousin, Commander-in-Chief Yin.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽中，爲太子領軍長史，官至廷尉。

translations.literal: During Song's Yuanhui era he was Chief Clerk of the Crown Prince's Pacification Army and rose to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song Yuanhui era he served as chief clerk of the crown prince's Pacification Army and rose to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 李珪之字孔璋，江夏鍾武人也。

translations.literal: Li Guizhi, courtesy name Kongzhang, was a native of Zhongwu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guizhi, courtesy name Kongzhang, was a native of Zhongwu in Jiangxia commandery.

sentences.zh: 父祖皆爲縣令。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather were both county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: His father and grandfather had both served as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 珪之少辟州從事。

translations.literal: Guizhi in youth was summoned as provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Guizhi was summoned to serve as a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，蔡興宗爲郢州，以珪之爲安西府佐，委以職事，清治見知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song's Taishi era, when Cai Xingzong was in Yingzhou, he made Guizhi a staff officer of the Western Pacification headquarters, entrusted him with duties, and his purity in governance won recognition.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song Taishi era, when Cai Xingzong governed Yingzhou, he made Guizhi a staff officer of the Western Pacification headquarters, entrusted him with important duties, and his clean administration won wide notice.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮西中郎諮議，右軍將軍，兼都水使者。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Consultative Officer of the Western Central Army, General of the Right Army, and concurrently Commissioner of Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to consultative officer of the Western Central Army, General of the Right Army, and concurrently Commissioner of Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 珪之歷職稱爲清能，除游擊將軍，兼使者如故。

translations.literal: In successive posts Guizhi was praised as pure and capable; he was appointed General of the Mobile Guard, retaining his concurrent commissionership as before.
translations.idiomatic: In successive posts Guizhi won praise for integrity and ability. He was appointed General of the Mobile Guard while keeping his concurrent post as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 轉兼少府，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent Minister of the Palace Supplies and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to concurrent Minister of the Palace Supplies and soon died.

sentences.zh: 先是，四年，滎陽毛惠素爲少府卿，吏才強而治事清刻。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fourth year, Mao Huisu of Xingyang was Minister of the Palace Supplies—strong in administrative talent and severe and exacting in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the fourth year, Mao Huisu of Xingyang served as Minister of the Palace Supplies. He was a strong administrator but stern and exacting in his methods.

sentences.zh: 勑市銅官碧青一千二百斤供御畫，用錢六十萬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the purchase of twelve hundred jin of azure pigment from the copper office for imperial painting, at a cost of six hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered twelve hundred jin of azure pigment from the copper office for imperial painting, at a cost of six hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 有讒惠素納利者，世祖怒，勑尚書評賈，貴二十八萬餘，有司奏之，伏誅。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Huisu for taking profit; Emperor Wu was angry and ordered the Secretariat to assess the price—it came to more than two hundred eighty thousand; the relevant offices memorialized and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Huisu of taking a kickback. Emperor Wu was furious and ordered the Secretariat to reassess the price, which came to more than two hundred eighty thousand. The relevant offices reported this, and Huisu was executed.

sentences.zh: 死後家徒四壁，上甚悔恨。

translations.literal: After his death the household was left with bare walls; the emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his home was left bare of possessions, and the emperor deeply regretted what had been done.

sentences.zh: 孔琇之，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Xiuzhi was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuzhi was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖季恭，光祿大夫，父靈運，著作郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jigong was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his father Lingyun was Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jigong was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his father Lingyun served as Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 琇之初爲國子生，舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi at first was a student of the Imperial University and was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi first entered the Imperial University and was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 除衞軍行參軍，員外郎，尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Guard Army, Outside-the-Capital Attendant, and Director of the Three Dukes Section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting adjutant of the Guard Army, outside-the-capital attendant, and director of the Three Dukes Section.

sentences.zh: 出爲烏程令，有吏能。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Wucheng and had administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Wucheng, where he showed real administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 還遷通直郎，補吳令。

translations.literal: On returning he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and supplemented as magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and appointed magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 有小兒年十歲，偷刈隣家稻一束，琇之付獄治罪，或諫之，琇之曰：「十歲便能爲盜，長大何所不爲？

translations.literal: A boy of ten stole and reaped one sheaf of a neighbor's rice; Xiuzhi handed him to prison for punishment; some advised against it, but Xiuzhi said: "At ten he can already steal—what will he not do when grown?"
translations.idiomatic: A ten-year-old boy stole a sheaf of rice from a neighbor's field. Xiuzhi had him imprisoned. When some urged leniency, Xiuzhi said, "If he steals at ten, what will he not do when he grows up?"

sentences.zh: 」縣中皆震肅。

translations.literal: " The whole county was awed into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole county was awed into discipline.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，又以職事知名。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and again became known for his official work.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and again won fame for his work in office.

sentences.zh: 轉前軍將軍，兼少府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Forward Army and concurrently Minister of the Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Forward Army and concurrently Minister of the Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，少府如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Valiant Cavalry, retaining his ministry as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Valiant Cavalry while keeping his post at the Ministry of Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、高宗冠軍征虜長史、江夏內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Chief Clerk of the Barbarian-quelling Champion General under the High Ancestor, and Interior Secretary of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk of the Barbarian-quelling Champion General under the High Ancestor, and Interior Secretary of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 還爲正員常侍，兼左民尚書、廷尉卿。

translations.literal: On returning he became regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Director of the Left People Section and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Director of the Left People Section and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 出爲臨海太守，在任清約，罷郡還，獻乾薑二十斤，世祖嫌少，及知琇之清，乃歎息。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Linhai; in office he was pure and sparing; when he left the commandery and returned he presented twenty jin of dried ginger; Emperor Wu thought it too little, but when he learned of Xiuzhi's purity he sighed.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Administrator of Linhai, governing with austerity. When he left office he presented only twenty jin of dried ginger as a gift. Emperor Wu thought it too little, but when he learned how incorrupt Xiuzhi was, he sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 除武陵王前軍長史，未拜，仍出爲輔國將軍，監吳興郡，尋拜太守，治稱清嚴。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Forward Army under the Prince of Wuling but did not take office; he then went out as General Who Supports the State, supervised Wuxing commandery, and soon was appointed grand administrator, his governance praised as pure and stern.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of the Forward Army under the Prince of Wuling but never took up the post. He was then sent out as General Who Supports the State to supervise Wuxing commandery and soon became grand administrator, winning praise for pure and stern governance.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：琴瑟不調，必解而更張也。

translations.literal: The historian says: When lute and zither are out of tune, one must loosen and restring them.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When the lute and zither are out of tune, they must be restrung.

sentences.zh: 魏晉爲吏，稍與漢乖，苛猛之風雖衰，而仁愛之情亦減。

translations.literal: Under Wei and Jin, serving as officials gradually diverged from Han practice; though the harsh and severe style declined, humane feeling also diminished.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, official service gradually diverged from Han practice. The harsh and severe style faded, but humane feeling diminished as well.

sentences.zh: 局以峻法，限以常條，以必世之仁未及宣理，而朞月之望已求治術。

translations.literal: They were confined by stern law and bounded by routine statutes, so that benevolence lasting generations had not yet been spread in governance while the hope of a month's term already demanded techniques of rule.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were hemmed in by harsh laws and routine statutes. The benevolence that should last generations had not yet been put into practice, yet within a single term in office they were already expected to show results.

sentences.zh: 先公後私，在己未易，割民奉國，於物非難，期之救過，所利苟免。

translations.literal: Putting public affairs before private interest was not easy for oneself; cutting the people to serve the state was not hard toward others; what was sought was remedy of faults, and the profit sought was mere escape.
translations.idiomatic: Putting the public good before private interest was hard for oneself, but cutting the people to serve the state was easy enough toward others. What was expected was merely to remedy faults, and the profit sought was only to escape blame.

sentences.zh: 且目見可欲，嗜好方流，貪以敗官，取與違義，吏之不臧，罔非由此。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the eye sees what is desirable, appetites begin to flow; greed ruins office, taking and giving violate right principle—there is no corruption among officials that does not arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the eye sees temptation, desire takes hold. Greed ruins office; taking and giving violate right principle. There is scarcely an instance of official corruption that does not spring from this.

sentences.zh: 擿姦辯偽，誠俟異識，垂名著績，唯有廉平。

translations.literal: Exposing wrongdoing and distinguishing falsehood truly await unusual insight; to leave a lasting name and manifest achievement, only integrity and fairness suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Exposing crime and distinguishing falsehood truly require exceptional insight, but to leave a lasting name and manifest achievement, only integrity and fairness will do.

sentences.zh: 今世之治民，未有出於此也。

translations.literal: In governing the people today, nothing goes beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people today, nothing goes beyond this principle.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：蒸蒸小民，吏職長親。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The teeming common people—the official's duty is to be their elder and kin.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The teeming common people look to officials as elders and kin.

sentences.zh: 棼亂須理，卹隱歸仁。

translations.literal: Tangled disorder must be set right; comforting the hidden brings return to benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Tangled disorder must be set right; comforting the suffering leads back to benevolence.

sentences.zh: 枉直交瞀，寬猛代陳。

translations.literal: Crooked and straight mingle in confusion; lenience and severity succeed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong mingle in confusion; lenience and severity take turns in office.

sentences.zh: 伊何導物，貴在清身。

translations.literal: What guides all things? The precious thing is a pure person.
translations.idiomatic: What guides the people? The precious thing is integrity in the official himself.
